question: At very high temperatures (e.g., $> 500$ K), an extrinsic (doped) semiconductor behaves increasingly like an intrinsic semiconductor. What is the physical reason for this transition?

options.A: The dopant atoms vaporize and leave the crystal lattice.
options.B: The dopant atoms become neutral again and stop contributing carriers.
options.C: The thermally generated intrinsic carriers ($n_i$) far outnumber the constant dopant-generated carriers.
options.D: The mobility of the charge carriers becomes zero due to lattice vibrations.
